newsitem.title: GERMANY: German state to probe inside trade in steel merger.
newsitem.headline: German state to probe inside trade in steel merger.

text.p: The German state of North Rhine-Westphalia said on Friday it would initiate a probe into possible insider trading offences linked to steel group Krupp's hostile takeover bid for its rival Thyssen.
Speaking to the Thyssen works council at a public gathering, Heinz Schluesser, the Social Democratic (SPD) state finance minister, said there were many holes in German secuurities law.
"But the responsible parties have to exercise due diligence," he said.
German state to probe inside trade in steel merger
Prior to Krupp's bid this week, Thyssen shares were up nearly 27 percent since the beginning of the year and have continued rising sharply since the takeover move was launched this week.

Thyssen shares closed bourse trade up four percent at 391 marks on Friday. Krupp had offered to pay Thyssen shareholders 435 marks a share but put the offer on ice after it agreed to begin talks with Thyssen about merging their steel companies.
Schleusser has been harshly critical of German banks since Fried. Krupp AG Hoesch-Krupp this week launched a rare hostile takeover bid for its larger rival Thyssen.
The finance minister has complained that while Deutsche Bank has a seat on the Thyssen supervisory board, it also advised Krupp in its takeover attempt, an apparent conflict of interest.
Krupp is being advised in its efforts by Deutsche Bank, Dresdner Bank and U.S. investment house Goldman Sachs, and other unidentified financial institutions.

State politicians and the IG Metall metal workers union have fiercely attacked the banks for their support of Krupp's bold takeover attempt, a rare move in Germany where mergers are usually cordially arranged.
Thyssen, while saying it still regarded Krupp's advances as hostile, denied that any member of its supervisory board was engaged in any wrong-doing.

The company said in a statement that it "placed value on stating that allegations raised in the public ... against individual members of the Thyssen AG supervisory board and their actions during board meetings do not reflect the facts."

The BAWe securities trading watchdog in Frankfurt said it was not planning a special investigation into the movements of Thyssen shares, but added that as a matter of course it always probes share movements related to any merger.
